object_description: four staggered buildings with oversized gable roofs
design_condition: Four staggered buildings reduce in height toward the church and organize a school square, but the courtyard orientation, cemetery edge, sloping site, and relationship to the existing gymnasium remain problematic.

positive.statement: The clear analysis of the local development situation leads to a coherent interpretation with four staggered buildings.

position.rationale: Four distinct staggered masses are clearly visible in plan and elevations.

positive.statement: The easily usable school square leads directly to the village square via a staircase.

position.rationale: Open space between masses is visible near the lower, street-facing side.

positive.statement: The organizational arrangement solves the essential processes well to very well internally.

position.rationale: Interior processes are approximated within the larger sampled building volumes.

positive.statement: The chosen arrangement allows the desired flexibility in the school building.

position.rationale: Flexibility is assigned to the eastern school volume, without distinguishable interior markers.

positive.statement: The supporting structure, statics, and foundation are described in detail and plausibly.

position.rationale: Structural judgment is anchored to the visible building footprints and ground contact.

negative.statement: The rectangular and overly high gable roofs integrate poorly into the existing townscape and appear out of place in their materialization.

position.rationale: Tall rectangular roof forms are clearly visible above the eastern mass.

negative.statement: The orientation of the inner courtyard towards the cemetery is likely to be problematic.

position.rationale: The courtyard is approximated in the gap between masses toward the northern edge.

negative.statement: The connection to and architectural treatment of the existing gymnasium is hidden, so the desired uniform appearance breaks apart.

position.rationale: The likely connection is placed at the detached eastern volume’s inward-facing edge.

negative.statement: The use of the break room and outdoor school room adjacent to the cemetery seems questionable.

position.target: break room and outdoor school room adjacent to cemetery
position.rationale: Adjacency to the cemetery constrains this estimate along the northern site edge.

negative.statement: The open space facing the street pays little attention to the sloping elevation and develops no concrete statement about it.

position.rationale: Street-facing open space is placed along the southern foreground edge of the site.

negative.statement: No statements are made about sun protection, and the facade treatment is not convincing for summer heat protection.

position.target: summer heat protection and facade treatment
position.rationale: The south-facing envelope provides the most relevant approximate facade anchor.

negative.statement: No further statements are made regarding the sound problems arising when instruments are used in a wooden structure.

position.rationale: Acoustic concern is assigned to the visible upper structure of the school volume.

negative.statement: The project loses clarity in the site setting and the resulting outdoor spaces, and its overarching integration is not convincing.

position.target: site setting and resulting outdoor spaces
position.rationale: The overall arrangement and fragmented outdoor spaces are visible across the site plan.
